metadata.title: Gated exciton fluids IV: three heuristics tested and not confirmed: dimensional lifting, sliding walls, and completely monotone relaxation as a 3D mesh generator
metadata.description: Fourth paper of the gated-exciton line (I: 10.5281/zenodo.23294615; II: 10.5281/zenodo.23297479; III: 10.5281/zenodo.23298292). Three heuristics suggested for the classical node-arrangement problem were pre-registered and tested with a plain numpy L-BFGS engine on the container geometries of the Fenris study. E1, dimensional annealing: lifting particles to 2+k dimensions and annealing the extra coordinates away shows no benefit at equal compute in any of nine shape-kernel cases (30 starts each); lifted runs are 6-17 times more expensive and some leave the container (counted as failures). E2, sliding walls: the registered gate (a decrease of at least two in the number of non-sixfold nodes on at least three of six shapes) is not met: it is met on one shape and the disc gets significantly worse. E3, completely monotone relaxation as a 3D mesh generator: in a periodic cube (N=216, 30 paired starts) it is far better than Poisson points but slightly worse than Lloyd/CVT in the 5th-percentile tetrahedron radius ratio (0.63 vs 0.68; gate not met). All results are small-scale and classical; no claim about excitons, string theory or the universal-optimality theorem. Three dated amendments are disclosed, including a discarded partial run made with a slow code path. Written by an AI system; checked by independent instances; not refereed.
metadata.notes: Standalone paper of the SocrateAI-Scientific-QuantumFluids programme, written by an AI system under the author's standing instructions. Source archive: exploration/exciton and paper sources as committed. Repository state: git tag exciton-gated-4.
